importance_ranking.reason: High visual variation between PEB portal frame, conventional MS truss, insulated sandwich panel, and tin shed sub-types — buyers use the listing image to identify structure type before reading any text. Wrong structure type shown = immediate skip regardless of specs or price.

Span width, structure type, and cladding material are primary shortlisting gates — a seller who cannot deliver the required clear span or structure type is eliminated before any other consideration. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated for a capital construction project.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant consumer-facing brand with buyer recall in this category — market is fragmented across regional PEB fabricators and contractors; buyers search by spec, project portfolio, and IS compliance, not manufacturer brand name.
importance_ranking.reason: Warehouse shed procurement is a high-value construction project — buyers evaluate fabricator credentials, IS 800:2007 compliance, past project portfolio, turnkey capability, and erection track record during vendor selection. Company identity is a significant trust signal but evaluated after spec shortlisting.

Per sq ft rate varies substantially with span width, structure type, and cladding specification — price is only comparable after spec equivalence is confirmed. Indian buyers are price-aggressive and use listed rates as a budget entry point, but final price is always negotiated for large projects.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Some sellers quote per project (lump sum) for large turnkey contracts — per sq ft vs per project creates real price comparison confusion. Per sq ft is the dominant and preferred unit and must be shown alongside price.
importance_ranking.reason: Price cannot be compared across listings without knowing whether the rate is per sq ft or per project (lump sum). This ambiguity is a documented market reality in Indian warehouse shed procurement and materially affects buyer price interpretation.
